flagship_directive: Construct a finite-section Wiener–Hopf estimator with approximation error negligible relative to sampling error, and prove root-n inference and simultaneous graph coverage on a fixed-margin stable restricted-strip class that genuinely includes cyclic, reciprocal, and self-exciting networks.
critique: The broad theorem proves population identification only for stable nonzero common-exponential laws whose generator restricted to im(A) satisfies the principal-log strip; it neither identifies models outside that strip nor characterizes their alias classes. For cyclic and singular feedback networks, the recovered finite-lag response must still be passed through an infinite-dimensional Wiener–Hopf solve, and no computable approximation, sampling rate, or confidence theorem is proved for that branch. Rank-adaptive estimation and simultaneous graph coverage are established only for the acyclic fixed-margin class, while one-lag minimality for chains and transitive triangles and sharp boundary adaptation remain open. The framing accurately discloses these limitations and does not claim the open questions as settled.
